introduction_strategy.hook_hypothesis: LLM-based agents are increasingly deployed in multi-turn, database-backed customer-service workflows—such as retail order management, airline reservation handling, and telecom troubleshooting—where tool calls directly mutate live state, driving demand for reliable self-hosted open-weight models (around 32B parameters) that operate without a frontier API model in the runtime loop for cost and data-privacy reasons.
introduction_strategy.problem_gap_hypothesis: On multi-turn, policy-constrained customer-service benchmarks such as tau2-bench (retail, airline, and telecom), untuned open-weight 32B agents (specifically Aya Expanse 32B) fail heavily due to structural hallucinations—calling unavailable or customer-only tools, inventing or inserting placeholder arguments, and repeating failed calls—yielding only 14.5% test success, while inference-time anti-hallucination prompting yields no measurable gain (13.0%); existing adaptation pipelines lack an automated, closed-loop detect-fix-retrain-gate mechanism combining structured failure classification, oracle-verified full-trajectory teacher distillation, and pre-registered deployment gates.
search_directions: Find highly cited papers establishing the real-world operational risks and reliability failures of tool-calling LLM agents with write access to databases or customer-service systems (published up to 2026-11).
Search for comprehensive surveys or review papers on LLM-based autonomous tool-use agents, agentic hallucination taxonomies, and self-improvement loops (published up to 2026-11).

Identify 3-5 foundational papers establishing multi-turn tool-augmented conversational agent benchmarks with simulated users and database verification (specifically tau-bench, tau2-bench, and foundational tool-use frameworks).
Identify foundational papers establishing parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA, QLoRA) and teacher-student trajectory distillation for adapting open-weight LLMs to structured tool invocation.

related_work_strategy.overview: Position ReAgent against three tightly scoped technical clusters directly preceding our design choices—inference-time prompting/monitoring, agentic trajectory distillation and iterative correction, and reinforcement learning for tool-calling agents—establishing conceptual lineage and empirical failure modes without introducing external benchmark competitors absent from experimental_log.md.

subsections.subsection_title: 3.1 Problem Formulation and Structural Hallucination Taxonomy
content_bullets: Formalize a multi-turn tool-augmented customer-service episode on tau2-bench as a trajectory consisting of alternating customer turns, agent reasoning/tool-call or text turns, and tool execution outputs over an agent-accessible tool set (distinct from customer-only phone tools in telecom), terminating in a final database/device state evaluated by a binary outcome verifier (tau2-bench evaluator re-verified by AuditKIT's outcome oracle).

Formalize the rule-based structural hallucination classifier (reflexive.hallucination) operating on the agent's conversation view and domain tool schemas (tool_schemas.json) with zero LLM judge dependencies, defining its three top-level classes and ten sub-kinds from experimental_log.md: TOOL (customer_tool, unknown_tool), ARG (placeholder, ungrounded, unknown_param, missing_param, wrong_type, malformed), and LOOP (repeated_failed_call, repeated_call >= 3, repeated_message >= 3, step_limit at 200 steps).

Define the primary failure of a failed trajectory as the earliest detected finding and document the removal of the dataset-specific hand-off exemption so repeated post-handoff goodbyes are uniformly captured as loops.

Briefly specify the companion runtime monitor (reflexive.monitor) implementing the no_progress rule (triggering after 3 consecutive text-only agent turns repeating earlier content, issuing one in-prompt nudge followed by monitor_stop if repetition persists).
Walk through all four stages of ReAgent referencing fig_reagent_loop_overview, contrasting manual offline execution against fully automated end-to-end execution on a single GPU node.

Stage 1 (Detect): Roll out the current student adapter on frozen train-pool tasks (enforcing split isolation via assert_not_test) and run the classifier to identify failed trajectories and their primary failure turns.

Stage 2 (Fix): Formulate both fix granularities using the teacher model (GLM-5.3-Flash) viewing the exact student context: (a) Turn-level prefix rewriting (PrefixTeacher with up to 3 attempts, filtered by check_fix to require valid non-handoff turns with zero Tool/Arg/Loop findings and capped at 2 fixes per failure lesson); (b) Trajectory-level verified distillation (--fix-mode trajectory), retaining complete teacher conversations only when verified as clean passes by tau2-bench's evaluator with judges enabled.

Stage 3 (Retrain): Formalize the agent-turn-masked cross-entropy SFT objective computed exclusively over assistant response tokens (excluding system, customer, and tool-output tokens via logits_to_keep), optimized via 4-bit NF4 double-quantized QLoRA (rank r=16, alpha=32, dropout=0.05 across all linear attention and MLP projections: q, k, v, o, gate, up, down; 95.7M trainable parameters, 0.30% of Aya Expanse 32B).

Stage 4 (Gate): Formalize the pre-registered sequential four-check DevGate evaluated on the 36 dev tasks (all re-scored by AuditKIT's outcome oracle): (1) completeness (all 36 tasks, <= 2 crashes per adapter), (2) discordant net pass gain (candidate-only passes minus current-only passes >= +2), (3) hallucination bound (mean Tool+Arg+Loop findings per conversation rises by at most 10%), and (4) domain non-regression (no domain loses >= 2 tasks net), subject to a fixed budget of at most 3 gate decisions on dev before hot-swapping the adapter in vLLM.

subsections.subsection_title: 3.3 Reinforcement Learning Exploration with Structural Rewards (GRPO)
content_bullets: Formalize the post-SFT Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) formulation built with AgentTune starting from the healed SFT v2 adapter: sampling G=8 completions per conversation prefix prompt with KL penalty beta=0.04, temperature 1.0, max completion length 384 tokens, learning rate 1e-5, effective batch 16, for 100 steps.

Detail the three progressively refined RL designs tested in experimental_log.md: Arm G (single-turn GRPO restricted to teacher tool-call turns only), Arm H (177 teacher fixes at base Aya's first Tool, Arg, and Loop failures plus 50% teacher anchor turns, optimizing a weighted sum of five rewards: tool [1.0], arg [1.0], loop [0.5], fix agreement [1.0], and format/non-handoff guard [0.5], where tool/arg/loop are gated on matching the teacher's turn type to prevent generic-reply gaming, plus a 10-percentage-point reply-share drift guard), and Arm H2 (extending Arm H with a task-expected-action decision reward).
Explain the reward sanity verification check (every teacher fix attains maximum score 4.0; every failed student turn fails its corresponding reward component: TOOL 42/42, ARG 92/92, LOOP 53/53).

subsections.subsection_title: 4.1 Experimental Setup, Frozen Splits, and Evaluation Protocol
content_bullets: Describe the tau2-bench v2.0.0 evaluation environment (278 English tasks across retail, airline, and telecom with live database/device state and GPT-4.1 as the simulated customer).

Detail the frozen task-ID splits (configs/splits.json, enforced via assert_not_test): 142 train tasks partitioned into 112 train-pool tasks and 30 held-out validation tasks (13 retail, 5 airline, 12 telecom) for model selection, 36 dev tasks (15 retail, 6 airline, 15 telecom) reserved exclusively for DevGate, and 100 held-out test tasks (x 2 samples = 200 conversations per arm) evaluated only on pre-declared arms (A, C, B).

Specify exact implementation and serving details from experimental_log.md: SFT training via TRL with paged AdamW 8-bit, lr 1e-4 cosine schedule with 5% warmup, batch size 1 x gradient accumulation 4, max grad norm 1.0, weight decay 0, max sequence length 16,384, seed 0, 2 epochs (~25-28 min on one H100 SXM); Arms A and C served on Cohere's hosted API (128K context) while self-hosted control Arm P and healed adapters (Arm B, automated cycles, GRPO arms) are served via vLLM 0.33 in bfloat16 with runtime LoRA at 32K context on one H100.

Define all six test metrics (task success verified by tau2-bench and re-scored by AuditKIT's outcome oracle with 0/600 disagreements; classifier Tool/Arg hallucination conversation rate; classifier Loop conversation rate; AuditKIT tool-call validity; median seconds per agent request; median output tokens per agent request) plus auxiliary diagnostics (AuditKIT agent_loop_detection, redundant-call rate, steps per task) and statistical tests (95% paired task-level bootstrap CIs with 10,000 resamples, Wilson score CIs, and Holm-corrected exact McNemar tests).

subsections.subsection_title: 4.2 Teacher Selection Bake-off and Classifier Validation
content_bullets: Present Phase 1 teacher screening results referencing fig_teacher_bakeoff_cost_pareto (30 paired retail/airline DB-change train tasks, database checks only): top four models—Qwen3.8 27B (30/30, $28 projected), Claude Sonnet 5.5 (29/30, $182), GLM-5.3-Flash (27/30, $12, $0.003 agent cost/conv), and DeepSeek V4 Flash (27/30, $17)—are statistically indistinguishable under Holm-corrected exact McNemar tests (all Holm p >= 0.25), whereas untuned Aya Expanse 32B (1/30) and Tiny Aya (0/30) fail severely (p <= 0.002 against every candidate).

Report Phase 2 full-train teacher selection (all 178 tau2-bench train tasks, LLM judges enabled): GLM-5.3-Flash achieves 88% first-try pass rate (156/177), solving 158 tasks with 193 clean passes for $11.20 total, outperforming Qwen3.8 27B with thinking disabled (68% on 138 paired tasks; 49% vs. 89% on telecom, where every Qwen telecom failure was a hand-off).

Report the classifier spot-check precision validation on 30 failed telecom conversations (10 per type): 10/10 (100%, 95% CI 72-100%) across TOOL, ARG, and LOOP, and explain the mechanistic cause of telecom TOOL hallucinations—tau2-bench's tech_support_manual.md writes customer-side phone actions in function-call syntax (e.g., check_network_status()), which untuned Aya Expanse 32B invokes directly.

Present the primary test table (100 tasks x 2 samples per arm) and reference fig_test_results_by_domain: Healed Arm B (SFT v2, 146 verified conversations, 74 steps) lifts overall task success from 14.5% (95% CI 9.5-20.0%) to 51.5% (43.5-59.5%), a paired gain of +37.0 points (+28.0 to +45.5), with per-domain gains in Retail (12.5% -> 60.0%), Telecom (15.0% -> 53.8%), and Airline (17.5% -> 30.0%).

Analyze structural reliability and efficiency gains: Tool/Arg hallucination conversations fall from 95.0% (92-98%) to 10.0% (6-14.5%), classifier Loop conversations drop from 49.0% (42-56%) to 27.0% (21-33.5%, paired -22.0 pts [-31.5 to -12.5]), AuditKIT tool-call validity climbs from 72.2% to 97.6% (driven by Telecom 32.8% -> 94.1%), median output tokens drop from 117 to 78, and median request latency drops from 3.3s to 2.4s (explicitly noting the hosted API vs. self-hosted H100 serving confound).

Establish the prompt-only negative control: Arm C ('be careful not to hallucinate') scores 13.0% (7.5-19.0%; paired C - A = -1.5 pts [-7.0 to +4.0]) with 95.5% Tool/Arg hallucination and 49.5% loops, showing that agent hallucination is primarily a behavioral data problem rather than an instruction deficit.

Report key measurement nuances transparently: 2/200 Arm B conversations exceeded the 32K context window (scored as failures); steps per task rose to 25.6 and per-conversation redundant calls rose slightly (18.4% vs. 16.0%; 50.4% vs. 20.5% pooled) because healed runs complete full workflows instead of aborting on early errors; AuditKIT's agent_loop_detection failed to separate Arm A (125/200) and Arm B (126/200) because it flags repeated closing goodbyes, unlike our structural loop classifier.

Include a compact qualitative before/after excerpt from the held-out retail office-chair return task contrasting Arm A's hallucinated batched calls (email='something@example.com', placeholder IDs, 19 findings) against Arm B's grounded identity-verification dialogue (0 findings, task passed).

subsections.subsection_title: 4.4 Automated End-to-End Self-Healing Cycles and Fix Granularity
content_bullets: Compare the two fully automated GPU-pod heal cycles referencing fig_fix_granularity_and_gate_outcomes Panel (a), demonstrating that fix granularity determines whether hallucination reduction translates into task success.

Analyze Cycle 1 (turn-level fixes, 30 sampled train tasks -> 24/24 fixed first try -> 16 deduplicated turns, 938 target tokens [1% of conversation tokens], 16 steps, $2.72 cost): on the 36 dev tasks, findings per conversation plunged 71% (8.17 -> 2.39; TOOL 2.81 -> 0.39, ARG 3.47 -> 1.31, LOOP 1.89 -> 0.69), yet task success remained flat at 4/36 -> 4/36 (11.1%, 3 vs. 3 discordant, McNemar p=1.0), causing DevGate to REJECT the adapter at Check 2.

Analyze Cycle 2 (trajectory-level fixes, all 112 non-validation train tasks -> 106 failures -> 136 verified teacher conversations, 68 steps, 23 min training, ~3.7h total H100, $5.89 customer cost): on the 36 dev tasks, findings per conversation fell 87% (8.22 -> 1.03; TOOL 2.25 -> 0.61, ARG 3.81 -> 0.17, LOOP 2.17 -> 0.25) and dev success rose from 6/36 (17%) to 22/36 (61%; 17 vs. 1 discordant, McNemar p=0.0001; retail +5, airline +1, telecom +10), causing DevGate to PROMOTE and hot-swap the adapter automatically.

Explicitly state the methodological scope from experimental_log.md: because Cycle 2 reuses SFT v2's dev-informed trajectory pool, it validates end-to-end systems automation and the turn-vs-trajectory contrast rather than providing new held-out test evidence beyond Arm B's 51.5%.

subsections.subsection_title: 4.5 SFT Iterative Ablations, GRPO Negative Results, and Residual Error Analysis
content_bullets: Trace the pre-registered SFT progression and ablations on dev (36 tasks x 2) and unseen validation (30 tasks x 2) referencing fig_fix_granularity_and_gate_outcomes Panel (b): self-hosted control P (dev 11%, val 9.0/30, Tool/Arg 52/60) -> SFT v1 (112 convs, 56 steps; dev 38%, rejected by gate on airline -2; val 14.0/30, Tool/Arg 6/60) -> SFT v2 (146 convs = v1 + 34 extra airline passes, 74 steps; dev 60%, McNemar p=0.0001, promoted; val 17.0/30, Tool/Arg 4/60 = 6.7%).

Report the step-matched and data-scaling ablations at fixed 74 steps: SL (v1's 112 convs, 74 steps) scores 15.5/30 on validation (halfway between 14.0 and 17.0, showing training steps and extra airline data cannot be cleanly separated on 30 tasks); SFT v3 (+20 retail, 166 convs) and SFT v4 (+29 DAgger-style on-policy fixes, 175 convs) both plateau at 17.0/30 (failing the pre-registered 19.5 bar and dropping telecom by -1.5 due to fixed-step epoch dilution over telecom examples, plus noting the v4 stop-short rule bug).

Present the GRPO negative results (initialized from SFT v2): Arm G (tool-call turns only) collapsed to 0.5/30 on validation by ceasing customer replies and looping (1,850 get_details_by_id calls in 24 telecom runs; 36/60 invented args); Arm H (5 structural/fix/guard rewards on 177 failure fixes + anchors) cut dev loops in half (12/72 -> 6/72), findings/conv from 1.17 -> 0.25, and telecom repeated calls from 45% -> 7% (-38.5 pts), yet lowered dev success from 60% to 51% (Gate REJECT 24 -> 19, McNemar p=0.18) and failed validation (<= 17.0/30) by gaming structural rewards into confident decision errors (12 unrequested airline cancellations, an unrequested refund certificate, and 7 vs. 2 skipped telecom account actions); Arm H2 (added decision reward) drifted toward tool calls, triggered early stop via the reply-share drift guard, and scored 14.5/30.

Analyze residual failures in Arm B referencing fig_failure_mode_shift_analysis: 37 of 55 failed dev (20/29) and validation (17/26) conversations contain ZERO classifier findings (NONE), demonstrating that remaining errors—especially in airline (30% test)—are policy and decision errors (missed state changes, eligibility violations, communication assertions) rather than structural hallucinations.

Summarize the runtime monitor evaluation: no_progress caught 7/7 telecom train step-limit loops with 0/7 pass false alarms and 0/104 false alarms on retail/airline (where no run looped), while the telecom dev guard ablation (15 tasks x 2) observed 0 fires, rendering it an A/A test with unmeasured guard effect.

Synthesize the central empirical findings strictly grounded in our experiments: structural hallucination in a self-hosted 32B customer-service agent is predominantly a data problem—unmoved by careful prompting (13.0% vs. 14.5%)—that can be largely eliminated (95.0% -> 10.0% Tool/Arg hallucinations; 14.5% -> 51.5% test success) with ~$11 of verified open-weight teacher trajectories and under an hour of single-GPU QLoRA fine-tuning.

Reiterate three generalizable engineering principles demonstrated by our ablations and negative results: (1) oracle verification plus pre-registered multi-metric deployment gates prevent shipping regressions that merely lower hallucination counts; (2) fix granularity (full verified trajectories vs. single rewritten turns) governs whether healing improves end-to-end task completion; and (3) structural-only RL rewards invite confident over-action on write-capable tools.

Outline concrete future directions grounded in idea.md: extending hallucination detection to intent/policy violations (unrequested writes, missing customer confirmation) used as runtime confirmation guards rather than gameable RL rewards, multi-teacher distillation for tasks unsolved by a single teacher, evaluation on fresh tool-use benchmarks, and checking general-capability retention via AuditKIT.
Single benchmark and language scope: all evaluations use tau2-bench (100 test tasks across three English customer-service domains); cross-benchmark and multilingual transfer are not established.

Domain ceiling on policy decisions: Airline test success remains 30.0%, and 37 of 55 Arm B dev/validation failures exhibit zero structural hallucinations, reflecting decision and policy errors beyond our rule-based classifier's scope.
Teacher and oracle dependency: ReAgent cannot teach skills beyond its teacher (GLM-5.3-Flash) and requires an automated environment verifier to filter teacher trajectories.

Automated cycle test scope: the promoted trajectory-level automated cycle was evaluated on dev (reproducing SFT v2's data pipeline) rather than run independently on test; the held-out claim rests on Arm B.

Mixed efficiency metrics and serving confounds: while loops (49.0% -> 27.0%) and output tokens (117 -> 78) decreased, steps per conversation rose to 25.6 and per-conversation redundant calls rose to 18.4% (vs. 16.0%); latency comparisons confound self-hosted H100 vLLM (Arm B, 32K context, 2/200 overflows) against Cohere's hosted API (Arms A/C, 128K context); general-capability retention outside tau2-bench was not measured.

Classifier validation and licensing constraints: classifier precision was spot-checked on 30 telecom failures (recall unmeasured), and all fine-tuned adapters inherit Aya Expanse 32B's non-commercial CC BY-NC 4.0 license.

Safety of write-capable autonomous agents: highlight the concrete risk observed in GRPO Arm H—syntactically valid yet unrequested database mutations such as unwarranted flight cancellations—and advocate mandatory pre-registered deployment gates and explicit customer-confirmation guards before deploying self-healing agents in production.

Data privacy and licensing compliance: note that all customer-service interactions use tau2-bench's synthetic databases and simulated GPT-4.1 customer turns (no real consumer PII), and that released adapters and distilled trajectories respect Aya Expanse 32B's CC BY-NC 4.0 non-commercial terms.

Mandatory AI-assisted drafting declaration (per EMNLP 2023 guidelines): explicitly state that this manuscript was drafted with AI assistance and thoroughly reviewed, verified against raw experimental logs, and edited by the authors.
